blockers.message: the review record has no `## code.review` section, while roles were active at it

findings.evidence: - A plugin system for export formats, so that PDF, XLSX, XML and JSON exports can be added later by dropping a module in `src/export/plugins/`.
findings.recommendation: The Why only asks to stop accountants copying invoices one by one into their spreadsheet; one CSV export answers it. Drop the plugin system from What Changes, replace "Decision: Exports go through a plugin registry" in design.md (whose only rejected alternative, "a single CSV function (not extensible)", is the simpler design the Why calls for), and remove task 1.2 with its `npm test -- registry` check. Start-up discovery of modules in `src/export/plugins/` also rests on an unverified assumption about how the `tsc`-built server loads files; it disappears with the registry.
findings.title: Plugin system for export formats nobody asked for

findings.evidence: The settings page SHALL let a user choose their preferred export format among the installed plugins.
findings.location: specs/invoice-export/spec.md#Requirement: Users choose their export format
findings.recommendation: Nothing in the Why asks for a per-user format preference, and with CSV as the only format there is nothing to choose. Remove the requirement and its scenarios, the settings-page bullet of proposal.md#What Changes and `web/src/settings/` from Impact, the sentence "A settings page stores each user's preferred format." in design.md, and task 2.1. As written, the scenario "A preference" (THEN exports use CSV) cannot be checked either: the only route is `GET /invoices.csv`, so the preference changes nothing observable.
findings.title: Settings page for a preferred export format nobody asked for

findings.recommendation: The new route `GET /invoices.csv` exposes every invoice of a month, including customer names, and the plan modifies the settings page; yet every domain is unticked with no reason. Tick security and personal-data (so their experts review who may export and what customer data leaves the system), and tick user-interface while the settings page stays in scope — or give each unticked domain its reason on its line.
findings.title: Domains all unticked while the plan exposes invoice data and changes a page

findings.evidence: `GET /invoices.csv?month=YYYY-MM` SHALL return the month's invoices, one per line after a header line, with number, date, customer and total; a field holding a comma, a quote or a line break SHALL be quoted as RFC 4180 says.
findings.location: specs/invoice-export/spec.md#Requirement: Invoices are exported as CSV
findings.recommendation: The scenarios cover a month, an invalid month, an empty month and a comma, but none says what happens when the request comes from someone who is not signed in or not allowed to see invoices; as written, any caller gets the whole month's invoices. State who may export and add a scenario for the refused caller, with its status code, and a matching test in task 1.1.
findings.title: Export requirement has no scenario for an unauthorized caller
